QIMING / FAQ

FAQ

Straight answers about setup, scope, membership, and credential handling.

What is Qiming Skill?

Qiming is a project-local AI work management Skill. It reads the files and rules in a directory you choose, then creates an entry so future agents can continue development, writing, site operations, or other long-running work.

How do I start if I am new to AI?

Prepare one folder and put your material there. Install the Qiming seed, then ask your agent in that folder: “$qiming Enable Qiming in this directory.” Give it one small task to do first.

Does installation automatically manage all my folders?

No. Installing the seed only makes adoption available. An independent instance is created only in a project you explicitly select. Existing names, files, and rules take priority.

Does “member” mean a paid subscription?

No. A member is a project, account, device, reusable script, Skill, program, or MCP that you maintain over time. Retained work records its owner and source; internal files stay with their parent member.

Where do my data and passwords live?

Project rules, tasks, knowledge, and tools remain in your own project directory. Account records refer to secure credential storage; ordinary project files do not contain passwords or keys.

Which agents have been verified?

Project adoption, binding, and remote installation have targeted verification with Codex. Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, and other operating system combinations still require individual real-world tests.
